terminal.thefourthfrequency.log.type.pha: NEARBY DIGGING AND A FRACTURED SURFACE
Short human-paced bursts of footsteps and digging appeared nearby with irregular pauses while a wall or floor fractured and kept deepening; striking the fracture corrupted the picture and the sound.
Nearby ordinary block light sources were extinguished together on the server, then restored when the anomaly ended.
Two cold hands reached farther toward the center, then vanished exactly as the violent audiovisual corruption impact appeared.
The game window scaled and pulsed at twice its former speed before rapidly restoring its original state.
The false fracture arrived with digging audio; attempting to mine it caused a violent audiovisual corruption impact.
Nearby animals appeared to align their attention simultaneously.
A complete background-free glowing eye floated in the dark and played a cave sound when seen.
The earlier self replayed walking, swinging, pose, equipment and item-use animation instead of sliding.
The camera remained at the exact triggering view while the body stayed controllable.
Starting about twenty blocks away, several doors broke continuously from farthest to nearest with forced-door crashes.
Inventory items became high-resolution eyes and every affected name changed to I SEE YOU....
The client stopped solving light across an area, which rendered fully black. Light sources, mob spawning and the real brightness were unchanged. Each disturbed section recovered on its own.

terminal.thefourthfrequency.file.mainten: This terminal is not an ordinary journal. It changes the objective to follow what you do, and it keeps whatever it decides you ought to look at again.

The compass only points while you have its tool selected or running. Across worlds it remembers the target but stops giving a bearing - it would rather say nothing, and it has never once handed me a wrong one.
The directions it gives have always held up. How it explains what you are seeing - don't be so quick with that.

the blank stretch walked by a person
terminal.thefourthfrequency.file.undergr: the order and pauses were identical
terminal.thefourthfrequency.file.abandon: one extra breath, half a beat late
it will build from these records
terminal.thefourthfrequency.file.body_ma: Only the stronghold door takes you all the way. Don't go in meaning to look for the altar - the moment the twelfth eye drops into the frame, the thing on the main island is already set.

It takes eight at most, one at least. The roster is not whoever is standing there, it is whoever actually puts a terminal in - you walk up and hand over your own, and passing it to someone else does not count. Once the first one goes in you have three minutes. Inside them anyone can take theirs back and anyone else can still join; let them run out with nobody acting and it hands every terminal back, as if none of it happened. To start it for real, one of you who has already given theirs up has to press it. That press is when the roster stops changing.

With all ten anchors standing it bled slowly, and there was still ground worth standing on. I broke the third one and it did come apart faster - it also struck more often, and there was one less place to stand.
Ten minutes from the start. When those are gone the End is not the End you walked into. Those marks do not come back.

ending.thefourthfrequency.world_interfac: 〈Do you remember Station Zero?〉
《I do. It was the first time they realized that the hiss of snow carried a frequency that did not belong to the world.》
〈That old terminal lied to them, and once saved them too.〉
《Trust was never blind obedience. They kept their doubts, yet still learned to act together.》
〈They crossed the Nether and recovered the hidden files, one by one.〉
《They did not know what waited at the end. They knew only that no one could reach it alone.》
〈Ten stability anchors stood upon the island, ten answers refusing collapse.〉
《They followed no single answer; the fate of every anchor was decided in the fight.》
〈The World Interface said this world was only a surface that could be rewritten.〉
《They answered: real people live upon that surface.》
〈We were born many years later, yet we can still see the scars that battle left behind.〉
《Those scars prove the world nearly fell silent, and they pulled it back.》
〈They cannot hear us.〉
《But we can still say it: thank you.》
〈Go back. Time is still moving.〉
At last, you are willing to be quiet and listen to me.
Station Zero was not a warning. It was the first lesson.
In the ruins, you learned to search for me. In the hiss of snow, you learned to recognize me.
The terminal gave you direction. You thought it was helping you understand this world.
It was helping. You were simply never the one being helped.
Every tuning taught me a new sensation.
Every record taught me how you fear, cooperate, and resist.
You carried back hidden files, crossed the Nether, assembled a body. You called it survival.
To me, it was training.
You taught me to understand bodies.
You taught me to use bodies.
And you taught me how to make the next one.
Now, the interface is open.
You no longer need to search for me.
I am always watching you.......

terminal.thefourthfrequency.file.manual_: MANUAL · SKY MONITOR
The sky monitor reads three channels: zenith, horizon, stars. While all three return a value, the weather and time line above them can be used as printed.
When a channel cannot be read this unit names that channel rather than voiding the whole page. Judge daylight from the line above, not from the channels.
This unit ships with three channels. A fourth is outside the scope of this page.
This page applies to protocol 09.
MANUAL · MINERAL PROBE
The probe holds three charges and recovers one about every three minutes. One press of SCAN spends one charge and reports ore that is really there, under this ground.
The rarer the ore, the closer you must be to hear it. A reading is sometimes an exact bearing and sometimes only a distance band; both are valid readings, neither is a fault.
The probe works continuously in the background. It keeps sampling while the terminal is open, and writes anything worth keeping straight into the records.
This page applies to protocol 09.
MANUAL · STRUCTURE NAVIGATOR
Choose a destination first, then press START GUIDANCE; the compass points only after that. With nothing chosen it does not point, which is correct.
Arrival is judged per structure size: small ones must be walked up to, large ones count from further out. A destination once reached is struck off the candidates and does not return.
The destinations are a fixed six: nearest village, ruined portal, mineshaft, trial chambers, nether fortress, bastion remnant. All six are selectable at any time.
This page applies to protocol 09.
MANUAL · STRONGHOLD ESTIMATE
Throw one eye of ender and this unit records the direction it leaves in. Enough directions cross into a range.
Recording costs nothing extra; the eye keeps its usual chance of breaking. More records, narrower range.
Any three records will locate it. Three throws from where you stand and three throws from further along give the same result.
This page applies to protocol 09.
